FacTweet detects the factuality of Twitter news accounts by modeling chronological chunks of their tweets with a recurrent neural network.
The paper addresses accounts that mix real and misleading news, proposing account-level detection as a potential pre-filter because tweet-level annotation is costly and time-consuming.
Tweets are sorted by posting date and split into chunks. The model applies attention to important tweets within each chunk, and an account’s label is the majority class of its chunks.
The model uses emotion, sentiment, morality and stylistic features, along with pretrained word embeddings.
The dataset draws on previously annotated lists of non-factual and independently considered trustworthy accounts. The authors excluded satire, some non-English accounts, and duplicate, media-based and link-only tweets; they collected up to the maximum tweets allowed by the Twitter API per account.
FacTweet achieved 0.74 accuracy and 0.565 macro-F1 in account classification. Ablation tests indicated that most performance gains came from word embeddings, style and morality features.
The authors propose future work on how features change across timelines, explicit temporal information such as timestamps, and a multilingual version.

The silver data comes from the DISC corpus, created by querying emotion-related words. Because each tweet’s specific emotion was not public, the researchers compared DISC with their scraped tweets to assign emotions automatically.

The authors represent syntactic information using dependency heads and relation labels, or using paths between candidate arguments and predicates.
DEP represents the dependency head, normally by its corresponding word; in LISA, it is a one-hot matrix of head-word indices. REL represents the relation between a word and its syntactic head.
DEPPATH uses the Tree-based Position Feature, while RELPATH uses the Shortest Dependency Path. Both preserve information about the path between a candidate argument and predicate in the dependency tree.
To construct the paths, the authors find the lowest common ancestor and the sub-paths from it to the predicate and argument. DEPPATH concatenates the two distances; RELPATH concatenates the dependency labels along the two sub-paths.
DEP and REL are mapped from strings into dense vectors, as are DEPPATH and RELPATH.
The authors also present input concatenation, which adds syntax embeddings to the neural network’s original inputs.
Their LISA-based approach replaces one attention head’s softmax matrix with a one-hot dependency-head matrix during training and testing, and adds dependency-relation information to that head’s values.
Relation-aware self-attention adds dependency-head and relation information to the queries and values in each attention head, capturing pairwise relationships between input elements.
